profiles.title: Utah: isolated out-of-plane silicon needles
profiles.summary: Two perpendicular saw passes create needles normal to the wafer. Glass isolates their roots. Height pattern, conductive site exposure and the connector map are independent decisions; neither a 10 × 10 array nor an intact tip guarantees 100 wired channels.

variants.label: Uniform-height Utah / NeuroPort comparison
variants.description: Jones’ glass-isolated geometry is the process reference. A 100-position, 96-connected example uses its own documented package map.

variants.label: Utah Slant, 400 µm pitch
variants.description: A row-dependent height profile changes handling and tip exposure. Blackrock lists 16–96 channels; use the ordered assembly map.

variants.label: HD-USEA research comparison
variants.description: Wark reports a distinct 25 electrodes/mm² arrangement. Do not shrink a 400 µm commercial route and assume the same process window.

variants.label: Earlier junction-isolated prototype
variants.description: A junction-isolated base is an alternative material architecture, not a glass-filled array with glass disabled. Its doping/thermomigration route is outside this glass workflow.

steps.title: Register wafer faces and array coordinates
steps.detail: Keep the pad-side coordinate origin, needle-side view and row-length vector distinct. A mirror transform appears when the die is flipped.
steps.check: An asymmetric corner mark must land on the correct pad after two flips.

steps.title: Cut or pattern the root isolation grid
steps.detail: Define channels between future conductive silicon roots on the backside. This grid is not the deeper needle-forming cut.
steps.check: Cross-sections show continuous silicon islands separated at each planned boundary.

steps.title: Fill the grid with insulating glass and expose the roots
steps.detail: The glass-silicon composite supports isolated columns. The original vacuum glass-filling setup is not a qualified process on the register; polishing and cross-section inspection represent only the finishing steps.
steps.check: Reject a conductive bridge or a void traversing the isolation region; measure between adjacent root pads.

steps.title: Register backside metal and the front height envelope
steps.detail: Locate each bonding pad on its isolated island. For the slant branch, a defined height pattern precedes or accompanies formation of the columns; its exact production fixture is not public.
steps.check: The pad footprint stays on a single island; row heights vary only on the selected slant branch.

steps.title: Saw columns, then shape tips
steps.detail: Orthogonal front-side cuts determine pitch and the inter-column clearance. Subsequent silicon shaping rounds and tapers the sawn posts; die-edge and interior posts can differ.
steps.check: Compare the tip and root geometry at center and perimeter. Do not transfer equal-height wafer etch uniformity to a slant part.

steps.title: Metallize, insulate and expose active tips
steps.detail: Separate tip conductor from dielectric sidewall, then expose only the intended area. Coating and de-insulation options depend on the array generation; the HD research paper compares two exposures.
steps.check: Record exposed area and sidewall breaches per needle. A large contact can lower impedance while indicating unwanted sidewall exposure.

steps.title: Map package leads and electrically screen
steps.detail: A bench map binds the physical (row,column) to the connected pad/pin; unused sites stay unconnected. Preserve the original package-specific mapping rather than assigning channels in geometric order.
steps.check: Keep physical count, connected count, open circuits, adjacent leakage and site impedance at the stated frequency as separate readouts.

gaps: No validated vacuum glass-reflow or proprietary production fixture is implied by a box furnace, dicing saw or wet bench.
The Utah geometry simulator is an educational subset, not a hardware qualification or electrical recorder. HD excimer optics are not the generic picosecond laser.

sources.title: Jones, Campbell & Normann (1992): glass/silicon composite array
sources.note: The authors distinguish isolation by glass from the junction isolation in an earlier array and report the 10 × 10 structure.

sources.title: University of Utah: three-dimensional electrode device
sources.note: Figures 6–13 and fabrication description: kerfs, dielectric filling, machining, surface contacts and insulation. A public example, not the current vendor traveler.

sources.title: Bhandari et al. (2010): wafer-scale shank etching
sources.note: Array dicing, isotropic shaping, spatial nonuniformity and surrounding sacrificial features on an equal-height wafer-scale demonstrator.

sources.title: Blackrock: Utah Slant Array
sources.note: Manufacturer’s slanted array geometry and connection options; site pitch and addressable count are distinct.

sources.title: Blackrock: NeuroPort Electrode user instructions, rev. 3
sources.note: Instrument identity and example electrode mapping, not a release of foundry masks or a manufacturing recipe.

sources.title: Wark et al. (2013): high-density Utah slanted array
sources.note: Research variant, 25 electrodes/mm²; optical and hybrid excimer/plasma tip-opening options. Not a default production Slant configuration.

profiles.title: Silicon microneedles with a removable tip mask
profiles.summary: The Semi-CAS process is not simply a Utah replica. Its tips touch PDMS during Parylene-C deposition. Removing the mask opens the contact mechanically rather than using a post-coat etch.

variants.label: 10 × 10 fabrication array
variants.description: Distinguish uniformity across the 100-position wafer-made array from the data of a separate smaller sample.

variants.label: 4 × 4 wired demonstration
variants.description: The smaller 16-channel device is not evidence that every electrode in an arbitrary 100-channel build is connected.

variants.label: Etch-opened tip in place of PDMS
variants.description: A valid comparison technology, but not the published local de-insulation branch.

steps.title: Define roots before front-side needles
steps.detail: On double-polished silicon, pattern and ICP-etch a backside pillar array. The resulting roots will become isolated conductors before the front-side shanks are shaped.
steps.check: Inspect island placement and depth on this face before flipping.

steps.title: Form silicon–glass backboard and pad contacts
steps.detail: Bond glass, allow the published glass-filling operation, then polish until conductive silicon ends are exposed. Pattern Cr/Au backside pads on those ends. Register machines represent bonding, polish and PVD roles only.
steps.check: A metal pad contacts one silicon end without bridging a glass boundary.

steps.title: Saw and sharpen the front pillars
steps.detail: Form the array of posts by orthogonal sawing, shape their tips by wet etching and deposit the front metal. Peripheral support features should not be counted as recording sites.
steps.check: Compare corner/edge and center profiles; confirm metal coverage at each intended tip.

steps.title: Exclude the tips during polymer coating
steps.detail: A controlled PDMS layer seats the ends while Parylene-C coats the shafts. Separating the mask leaves exposed ends; this is not oxygen-plasma removal.
steps.check: Measure exposed length distribution rather than treating a single approximately 50 µm value as a universal spec.

steps.title: Plate and package only the intended sites
steps.detail: Platinum black changes active area compared with bare Au. Wedge-bond insulated leads to a PCB, encapsulate the connections, and retain the defined channels for that package.
steps.check: Differentiate genuine low site impedance from shorted leads with a neighboring-site isolation check.

steps.title: Characterize the bench specimen
steps.detail: Compare masked contacts optically and collect impedance for Au and Pt-black finishes under matched conditions. The paper reports 33.2 kΩ at 1 kHz for its Pt-black sites: a comparison value, not a pass threshold for every part.
steps.check: Report individual sites, dispersion and missing measurements rather than extrapolating 16 channels to 100.

gaps: The anodic bonding, glass flow and PDMS insertion fixture need process-specific qualification; equipment-category names are not a guarantee.
The 4 × 4 biological demonstration is not simulated, and its neural yield is not assigned to a new batch.

sources.title: Zhao, Wei et al. (2025): local de-insulation of microneedle arrays
sources.note: Figure 1 process flow, de-insulation experiments and electrochemical characterization; the 100-position array and 16-channel demonstration are distinct.

profiles.title: Neuropixels 1.0: post-CMOS foundry to synthetic acquisition
profiles.summary: The public imec wafer-to-shank module order is known. It begins with a completed 130 nm foundry wafer, not blank silicon at the lab stepper. An electrical recording site and a digitizer channel are different objects.

variants.label: 1.0 production reference
variants.description: 10 mm shank; 960 sites, 384 selectable channels; manufacturer geometry is 70 × 24 µm in cross-section.

variants.label: 2017 published probe
variants.description: Jun et al. report a 70 × 20 µm shank in their implementation. Do not average paper and production thicknesses.

variants.label: Nonfunctional dummy
variants.description: A mechanical fit article cannot pass an electrical acquisition test.

steps.title: Accept completed foundry electronics
steps.detail: Track incoming wafer, top metal and die coordinates. The source explicitly starts with 200 mm wafers at a 130 nm node. The transistor stack and foundry design kit are external.
steps.check: Do not mark FEOL/BEOL manufactured merely because lithography or deposition tools exist in the register.

steps.title: Balance stress and open vias
steps.detail: The published sequence balances stress before via formation on 200 mm wafers. The registered 04-02 model accepts 100 mm, not this wafer. Full-wafer processing is external; no recipe or thickness follows from the module diagram.
steps.check: Measure wafer bow before/after compensation and test a via-chain witness; success on a smaller coupon does not qualify the production wafer.

steps.title: Define and protect electrode sites
steps.detail: Pattern the recording interfaces; TiN sites must stay connected to their corresponding electrical readout path. Protection separates site formation from later substrate processing.
steps.check: Overlay site windows against vias. An open via can disable one physical site without killing every site on the readout channel.

steps.title: Open pad windows and deep-etch front side
steps.detail: Open connection pads and define the front-side deep silicon boundary on the 200 mm workpiece. The registered 04-02 model accepts 100 mm and the 04-03 fixture 150 mm; neither represents this full-wafer etch.
steps.check: Keep pad exposure, outline continuity and clearance from active traces as distinct inspection gates.

steps.title: Thin and finish from the backside
steps.detail: Back-grind and deep-etch to complete the shank. A grinder cannot replace the final selective etch; the 150 mm 04-03 fixture cannot accept the source’s 200 mm wafer, so the complete production module remains external.
steps.check: Match the thickness to the selected production or paper configuration rather than accepting either value.

steps.title: Exercise a separately sized witness, not the 200 mm wafer
steps.detail: The listed tools illustrate deposition, openings and mechanical thinning on supported test pieces. A 100 mm carrier is the modeled 04-02 input; 04-03 requires its own 150 mm fixture. A coupon is a substitute test article only where a specific mount is qualified.
steps.check: Track dimensions and holder at each handoff. Never feed the 200 mm production wafer to these limited tools or use coupon measurements as its process record.

steps.title: Package and protect the base
steps.detail: Mount the die on its rigid board/flex and shield light-sensitive circuitry. The outsourced package drawing and build tolerances are not supplied by the module slide.
steps.check: Inspect bonds and compare dark and illuminated baselines without interpreting optical noise as neural signal.

steps.title: Verify selected sites with a known input
steps.detail: Apply a synthetic signal through the site map and compare expected AP/LFP streams. 384 live selections do not turn 960 sites into simultaneous channels.
steps.check: Move the selector away from a single disabled physical site, then back; distinguish site-local and channel-wide failures.

gaps: Exact masks, transistor deck, film stress targets, etch profiles, production yields and proprietary packaging remain outside the public reconstruction.
Zone 10-13 is a recording-system reference, not a CMOS fabrication tool.

sources.title: Majeed (imec), Neuropixels process flow, slide 11
sources.note: Slide 11 identifies the incoming 200 mm, 130 nm foundry wafer and four subsequent 1.0 modules. Slide 13 is a separate hybrid demonstrator, not the production 1.0 recipe.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

sources.title: Jun et al. (2017): integrated high-density silicon probes
sources.note: Design, Figure 1 and Methods distinguish physical sites, switch-selected channels and the separate AP/LFP digitization paths of the 2017 device.

sources.title: imec: probe, cable and headstage compatibility
sources.note: Product-specific order codes distinguish, among others, the Quad Base headstage/cable and the 1.0 and 2.0 systems.

profiles.title: Neuropixels 2.0 alpha: one- and four-shank paths
profiles.summary: The 2021 alpha is a monolithic switching probe. Changing the number of shanks changes the release geometry and the legal switch selections, but the probe still outputs 384 full-band channels in either configuration.

variants.label: Single shank · 1,280 sites
variants.description: Two vertically aligned columns. The 384-channel selection must respect 32-site mapping groups.

variants.label: Four shanks · 5,120 sites
variants.description: Four shanks at 250 µm center pitch share 384 readout channels. Documented patterns include 96 sites on each shank.

variants.label: 1,536-channel Quad Base
variants.description: This is a different base, headstage and channel allocation; it is not an alpha software mode.

steps.title: Choose the shank mask family and map
steps.detail: The 2021 single/four-shank layouts both use aligned 12 µm TiN squares; 15 µm row spacing along the shank differs from the staggered 1.0 layout. Geometry selects possible sites, not arbitrary channel wiring.
steps.check: Count 1,280 per shank. Verify that changing masks changes the outline and collection of valid site maps.

steps.title: Accept the 130 nm custom wafer
steps.detail: Shank switches and base readout are co-fabricated. The PDK, masks, electronics yield and post-processing recipe are not supplied by the alpha paper.
steps.check: Require a known tested base rather than assembling generic transistors in the probe lab.

steps.title: Define sites, compensate bow and release shanks
steps.detail: Compare TiN window registration and outline with the alpha data; thinning/deep-etch stations represent a plausible family route, not a demonstrated 2.0-specific process order.
steps.check: The alpha specification is a 70 × 24 µm section and less than 100 µm base-to-tip deflection for each shank, not an across-shank mean.

steps.title: Attach die to the alpha rigid-flex
steps.detail: Wire bonds and epoxy secure the base to the rigid PCB; the flexible ribbon connects the matching headstage.
steps.check: Inspect the bond fanout separately from the four physical shanks. An open package net may affect an entire stream.

steps.title: Exercise a valid selection against a dummy input
steps.detail: Use an alpha-compatible map. For a single shank, test an allowed contiguous block. For four shanks, test a legal 96-per-shank or same-shank selection. Read out 384 full-band streams; AP and LFP can be derived, not independent 1.0 ADC banks.
steps.check: Verify 30 ksample/s full-band sample timing, 14-bit alpha digitization and the same total channel budget for both options.

gaps: Do not apply the public 1.0 module sequence to 2.0 as a disclosed exact production process.
ASIC masks, proprietary back-end windows, generation-specific calibration and exact release fixtures remain external.

sources.title: Steinmetz et al. (2021): Neuropixels 2.0
sources.note: Methods, “Neuropixels 2.0 device design”: single/four-shank alpha variants, aligned sites, mechanical specifications, packaging and different maps. These results are alpha-specific.

sources.title: Majeed (imec), Neuropixels process flow, slide 11
sources.note: Slide 11 identifies the incoming 200 mm, 130 nm foundry wafer and four subsequent 1.0 modules. Slide 13 is a separate hybrid demonstrator, not the production 1.0 recipe.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

profiles.title: Neuropixels Ultra: dense-site switching window
profiles.summary: The studied Ultra trades sampled length for contact density without increasing the 384 simultaneous readouts. A 384-site window is an address pattern, not the full shank or the number of fabricated contacts.

variants.label: 48 × 8 dense window
variants.description: All eight columns sampled over 48 rows; 384 selected sites.

variants.label: 96 × 4 selection
variants.description: More rows and fewer selected columns; still 384 channels.

variants.label: 192 × 2 selection
variants.description: A longer, narrower sampling pattern.

variants.label: 384 × 1 selection
variants.description: Longest of the four stated patterns, without manufacturing a new die.

variants.label: Earlier 6,528-site or fixed 384-site revisions
variants.description: Separately described by the program; do not combine those counts with the studied 6,144-site device.

steps.title: Freeze revision and contact geometry
steps.detail: Choose the Ye et al. layout. On this die the 6,144 available sites are not all connected simultaneously. The dense window arithmetic is 48 rows × 8 columns.
steps.check: Store total physical sites, selection dimensions, row pitch and width of a site as separate fields.

steps.title: Accept external switch/readout die design
steps.detail: The 1.0-family readout and dense routing are not reproduced by direct writing an array of squares. Treat full upstream CMOS design and fabrication as supplied.
steps.check: A reference array with the same pitch is not labeled a functional Ultra.

steps.title: Check small contact openings and uniformity
steps.detail: Model patterning and TiN inspection on an interface coupon. A 5 µm square site on 6 µm pitch has 1 µm nominal edge clearance along aligned rows; overlay loss and unintended merging are distinct faults.
steps.check: Use the edge-to-edge clearance, not 6 µm, as the nominal gap. Reject shorted neighbors in a continuity mock-up.

steps.title: Reconstruct shank release and package envelope
steps.detail: Use a 1.0-like silicon shank/external readout as the reference, with mechanical checks independent of the electronics. Do not extrapolate a small contact crop into a recovered full mask.
steps.check: Match the shank form and selected revision. Log unknown die-outline and process tolerances.

steps.title: Verify the switching window with known signals
steps.detail: Replay a defined input using each documented 384-site layout. Changing software selection reallocates the existing channels; it does not change the manufactured site count.
steps.check: Each of 48×8, 96×4, 192×2 and 384×1 selects exactly 384 sites. No map produces 6,144 independent simultaneous signals.

gaps: The documented selection shapes are not a complete published wire-level netlist or a recovered foundry mask.
Earlier UHD revisions distinguished by Neuropixels Central are not evidence against the later study-specific count.

sources.title: Ye et al. (2025): Neuropixels Ultra
sources.note: Figure 1, Figure S1 and Methods: the reported 6,144-site version, 5 µm sites on 6 µm centers and selectable layouts.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

profiles.title: Neuropixels NHP: stitched long-shank silicon
profiles.summary: A 45 mm shank is longer than the exposure field. Its CMOS features must join at reticle seams. Widening lines and compensating film stress are structural changes, not a visual stretch of the rodent design.

variants.label: 45 mm study version · 4,416/384
variants.description: 125 µm wide, 90 µm thick, 4,416 selectable sites and 384 concurrent channels. The study used a beveled tip.

variants.label: 25 mm family comparison · 2,496/384
variants.description: The program also documents a shorter hardware variant; do not reuse the long probe’s stitch count or trace resistance.

variants.label: Scale up a 24 µm 1.0 rodent shank
variants.description: This does not implement the documented stiffness, pitch and reticle constraints.

steps.title: Tile a long die across exposure fields
steps.detail: The long probe is a monolithic die assembled lithographically from tip, repeated middle sections and base patterns. Overlapping exposures form electrical seams, not physically joined silicon parts.
steps.check: Overlay adjacent fields and check test conductors across every seam; a register stepper is only a visualization of this constraint.

steps.title: Receive custom stitched CMOS
steps.detail: The foundry forms the 130 nm SOI switching and readout circuits, with modified interconnect widths, isolation spacing, supply routing and decoupling.
steps.check: Keep stitch overlay, continuity and crosstalk on separate records. No full foundry masks are public here.

steps.title: Qualify the thinned, stress-balanced shank
steps.detail: Inspect for out-of-plane bow and thickness at multiple stations along the shank. Long-probe stress compensation and increased thickness must not be copied from rodent reference geometry.
steps.check: Use length-resolved data; the 45 mm study sample should not inherit a nominal 24 µm thickness.

steps.title: Inspect seams and optional side bevel
steps.detail: Compare the published two-axis tip and metal seam micrographs; study authors used a modified EG-402 grinder, not the registered stationary glass-electrode beveler.
steps.check: Log line narrowing separately from an actual open. Validate side bevel only for the documented sharpened version.

steps.title: Attach and exercise the readout on a fixture
steps.detail: Use the matched package and known electrical input to compare noise/coupling at sites near and far from a stitch. Do not simply repeat a rodent spectrum at every depth.
steps.check: Record the selected site’s position and channel. Limit to 384 concurrent channels for both listed lengths.

gaps: The register cannot qualify the 130 nm multilayer reticle stitching or reproduce the modified study grinder.
Probe geometry does not establish a fracture load or permit any biological performance prediction.

sources.title: Trautmann et al. (2025): long Neuropixels NHP
sources.note: Results, Technology, Figure 1 and Extended Data Figure 2: reticle stitching, 45 mm shank, stitch-line narrowing, bow compensation and tip grinding.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

profiles.title: Neuropixels 2.0 Quad Base: four fixed readout banks
profiles.summary: This device gives each of four shanks its own 384-channel base section. It differs both from a 384-total alpha probe and from the 1,536-channel NXT with movable capacity.

variants.label: Four banks of 384
variants.description: 5,120 physical sites, with at most 384 simultaneous selections per shank.

variants.label: Capped and uncapped ordering variants
variants.description: Use NP2020/NP2021-specific package drawings and accessory matching, not a change to site count.

variants.label: Move 912 channels onto one shank
variants.description: Not a Quad Base setting; NXT has a different switching architecture.

steps.title: Specify the four-section electrical architecture
steps.detail: Divide the 1,536-output contract into four shank-local sets; each 1,280-site shank supplies 384 valid connections.
steps.check: A selection asking for 385 independent channels on one shank fails even if the total stays below 1,536.

steps.title: Obtain dedicated device silicon
steps.detail: Upstream CMOS, masks, foundry integration, process controls and packaging tooling are not given by the buying specifications.
steps.check: Do not substitute four generic 2.0 dies for the documented device.

steps.title: Inspect shank quartet and package connectivity
steps.detail: Virtually check shank windows, alignment and all four bond groups; a 2.0-family CMP/etch route, if shown, remains an analogy rather than the Quad Base process record.
steps.check: Distinguish one failed site, one lost shank bank, and a completely unavailable headstage.

steps.title: Match the interface components
steps.detail: Use the dedicated HS_2020 headstage and CBL_2020 cable; the manufacturer lists PXIe_1000 or OneBox on the acquisition side.
steps.check: Reject a generic or standard alpha headstage match as unsupported; an acquisition chassis alone is not the interface.

steps.title: Check four bank maps and transport together
steps.detail: In a digital fixture, inject a unique tag per shank and check mapping, timestamps and sample counts separately across all four banks.
steps.check: Each bank outputs at most 384 independent tags; the full configured set has 1,536, not 5,120.

gaps: No vendor production masks or calibrated 4-bank wafer acceptance limits were identified.
Mechanical cap variants are not separate signal-processing architectures.

sources.title: imec: Neuropixels 2.0 Quad Base
sources.note: Manufacturer confirms four shanks, 1,280 sites per shank, 1,536 readouts and the dedicated HS_2020 interface.

sources.title: imec: probe, cable and headstage compatibility
sources.note: Product-specific order codes distinguish, among others, the Quad Base headstage/cable and the 1.0 and 2.0 systems.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

profiles.title: Neuropixels NXT: prototype and external foundry boundary
profiles.summary: The program reports a four-shank 1,536-channel prototype using 2.0 site geometry. SpikeGLX describes the NP3020 four-shank table fields. This is not a production traveler or proof that any set of sites below the capacity limit is routable on a particular prototype.

variants.label: Four-shank architecture
variants.description: The public description fixes total capacity; it is not a released list of every legal site tuple.

variants.label: Up to 912 on one shank
variants.description: A reported upper bound, not evidence that every arbitrary 912-site subset can be selected.

variants.label: Assume the 2.0 hybrid die-to-wafer demonstrator is the NXT recipe
variants.description: The separate imec report is not evidence that this exact prototype or product uses that complete process.

steps.title: Pin the prototype definition
steps.detail: Use the NXT/3.0 identity, four shanks and 2.0-style site geometry. Keep the revision/firmware field unspecified where public material is silent.
steps.check: Inventory entries for Quad Base and NXT must not alias to one hardware definition.

steps.title: Hold the upstream fabrication boundary
steps.detail: ASIC design, mask floorplan, layer order, PDK, interconnect details and wafer acceptance flow are not published in the program announcement.
steps.check: Do not convert slide 13 of a related imec demonstrator into an NXT production step.

steps.title: Inspect an interface coupon, not proprietary NXT silicon
steps.detail: Use metrology against disclosed shank geometry and known contacts only. Any local patterning/inspection is a teaching reference, not a cleared fabrication route.
steps.check: Geometry agreement without connectivity evidence never marks the external electronics path complete.

steps.title: Exercise reported capacity bounds
steps.detail: Validate a synthetic allocation against the public 1,536 total and up-to-912-on-one-shank statements. The NP3020 software table also needs shank, bank, reference and electrode identities. A channel count alone cannot validate such a table.
steps.check: Reject 1,537 total and 913 on one shank. Treat an otherwise bounded but undocumented set as unverified, not accepted hardware.

gaps: Revision-specific mapping validation, part-specific packaging and a verified production traveler are unavailable here.
A future release forecast does not demonstrate production yield or present availability.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: probe configurations and signal chain
sources.note: Program comparison of form factor, site selection, packaging and acquisition. Describes multiple Ultra generations and the NXT prototype separately.

sources.title: Neuropixels Central: NXT/3.0 access challenge
sources.note: Program announcement distinguishes prototype availability and future planned access from volume production.

sources.title: Majeed (imec), Neuropixels process flow, slide 11
sources.note: Slide 11 identifies the incoming 200 mm, 130 nm foundry wafer and four subsequent 1.0 modules. Slide 13 is a separate hybrid demonstrator, not the production 1.0 recipe.

sources.title: SpikeGLX: Imec readout table formats
sources.note: The public NP3020 software table specifies channel, shank, bank, reference and electrode fields. Format support does not identify a prototype revision or establish legal combinations from channel totals alone.

profiles.title: Neuropixels Opto: electrical shank with a photonic layer
profiles.summary: This is a fiber-fed photonic circuit above a 1.0 recording IC, not a row of bonded LEDs. The optical path and the electrode vias pass through different layers and need separate tests.

variants.label: 450 nm optical path
variants.description: One of 14 blue emitters; published blue-path loss and crosstalk differ from red.

variants.label: 638 nm optical path
variants.description: One of 14 red emitters; an emitter selection does not change the available 384 electrical readouts.

variants.label: Replace the fiber/switch tree with a bonded microLED
variants.description: An entirely different architecture that has no validity as an Opto configuration.

steps.title: Accept the recording IC
steps.detail: Six-metal 130 nm SOI aluminum CMOS carries the recording circuitry. The authors identify it as the 1.0 recording design; its transistor fabrication remains external.
steps.check: Do not infer a device-specific lithographic mask set from the probe’s public cross-section.

steps.title: Build the optical circuit above the CMOS
steps.detail: The 200 mm photonics flow adds shielding and a reflector, 150 nm PECVD silicon-nitride guides, grating couplers and heater-controlled switches. Its full-wafer etch is external: the register’s 04-02 model accepts a 100 mm input, not this wafer.
steps.check: Compare grating overlay and waveguide thickness separately from continuity of the buried readout.

steps.title: Reconnect the recording electrodes and manage bow
steps.detail: The added optical stack needs deeper vias for heaters and recording sites and a stress compensation layer. A complete 200 mm module is outside the verified 100 mm 04-02 model.
steps.check: Inspect the via-chain and released-shank bow independently; a light-output check cannot diagnose an open electrical via.

steps.title: Compare film, vias and bow on supported witnesses
steps.detail: Register deposition, etching and metrology can represent separate optical-film or via witnesses. The 04-02 software demonstration is 100 mm and does not validate photonic multilayer etching; the whole 200 mm wafer cannot be substituted.
steps.check: Tie each reported result to the specimen and method. A coupon’s thickness or continuity cannot qualify a 200 mm wafer or an optical switching tree.

steps.title: Prepare the tethered optical/electrical package
steps.detail: Align the fiber array to the couplers and connect the electronics. Electrical and optical ports require independent registration. A package die bonder is an analogy; it is not a verified multi-fiber alignment fixture.
steps.check: Read back an optical transfer measurement per port; a mechanically centered image is insufficient.

steps.title: Calibrate wavelength-specific routing
steps.detail: Compare selected-emitter output, neighboring-port leakage and propagation loss for each wavelength. The prototype’s blue leakage is a known limitation; do not silently use red extinction for blue.
steps.check: The paper measures full-probe loss with an integrating sphere. A meter console alone cannot collect total emitted power or establish insertion loss. Record collection method and wavelength for each result.

steps.title: Separate electronic and optical readouts
steps.detail: Apply an electronic calibration signal with light off, then evaluate a blank under optical switching. Keep the 960 physical sites, 384 electrical channels and 2 × 14 photonic emitters as independent counts.
steps.check: Optically induced artifact in a blank must not be labeled simulated neural activity.

gaps: CMOS masks, photonic PDK and detailed process traveler are not available. The published modules describe architecture, not a complete 740-step recreation.
Register lasers, optics bench and meter require the right source wavelengths, detector, coupling and return-path configuration.

sources.title: Lakunina et al. (2026): Neuropixels Opto
sources.note: Design and fabrication; Figure 1 and Extended Data Figure 1. Identifies the added photonic modules, fiber coupling, emitter layout, loss and prototype leakage.

profiles.title: Wise 1970: planar gold electrodes on an etched silicon carrier
profiles.summary: The 1970 article describes a passive probe made with integrated-circuit techniques. The unsupported gold recording end can project past the silicon carrier; there is no need to invent active transistors to explain the term “integrated-circuit.”

variants.label: Single-site probe
variants.description: The paper shows its cross-section and separate etched carrier.

variants.label: Multiple lithographic sites
variants.description: The same sequence with different masks yields multiple electrodes; the paper depicts the double-site example. No universal channel count is inferred.

steps.title: Start from oxidized silicon with two coordinate faces
steps.detail: The historical starting wafer was approximately 50 µm thick. Reference marks link the two faces before shaping. Thermal oxidation is an upstream supply/process boundary when its specific furnace is not registered.
steps.check: Test backside alignment on a witness: front and back marks must transform into the same projected coordinates.

steps.title: Etch the backside mesa and define oxide masks
steps.detail: A patterned backside oxide protects raised silicon during the first etch; reoxidation separates the carrier-shaping mask from the front insulating base.
steps.check: A backside topographic map distinguishes a partially formed mesa from a through-released carrier.

steps.title: Photoform the gold electrodes
steps.detail: The paper describes a plated and etched Au structure with thin nickel aiding adhesion to oxide. This differs from simply evaporating a flat Au film and calling it the historical contact. A qualified historical plating fixture is not in the register.
steps.check: Check continuous conductor from pad to tip; distinguish nominal gold width from its final exposed aperture.

steps.title: Insulate and selectively expose the tips
steps.detail: Top-side deposited oxide is selectively removed over recording ends; only the small contact area becomes electrolyte-accessible. A research PECVD station is a modern dielectric analogy, not the original RF apparatus.
steps.check: Inspect the aperture footprint and insulated shoulders, keeping the supporting oxide and surface overcoat distinct.

steps.title: Release by silicon undercut and package
steps.detail: The final isotropic silicon etch forms an overhang. Authors attached output wire by thermocompression, mounted it in a capillary handle and insulated the connection.
steps.check: Verify a projecting contact, distinct from an unwanted fractured tip; reject a connection leak even when the metal is continuous.

steps.title: Bench-check electrode versus interelectrode response
steps.detail: Use a defined electrolyte fixture and known input to distinguish individual site impedance from mutual coupling and leakage.
steps.check: For a two-site specimen, report a pair of site impedances plus the interelectrode measurement.

gaps: The register has no verified equivalent for the historical electroforming, oxidation and thermocompression stations.
This is the 1970 silicon carrier design, not a later Michigan boron etch-stop or CMOS probe.

sources.title: Wise, Angell & Starr (1970): integrated-circuit microprobe
sources.note: Section I.B, Figures 2–7: oxidized 50 µm silicon wafer, double-sided alignment, etched mesas, electroformed gold/Ni, top oxide openings and assembly.

profiles.title: NeuroNexus families: passive carriers, assemblies and active pixels
profiles.summary: Select the vendor family before assigning manufacturing steps. A planar passive array, two arrays bonded back-to-back, a 3D stack and an active-pixel ASIC cannot share a single finished-device traveler. Public academic flows are explicitly comparators.

variants.label: Passive planar / clustered sites
variants.description: One- or multi-shank masks with linear, tetrode or clustered contact layouts; exact geometry depends on the SKU.

variants.label: Fusion: two back-to-back arrays
variants.description: An assembly of two probes, not two-sided metallization on one monolithic wafer.

variants.label: Matrix: assembled 3D array
variants.description: Multiple planar arrays, assembled at a defined spacing. A top-view reticle alone is not the final geometry.

variants.label: SiNAPS active-pixel
variants.description: Active electronics require foundry silicon. An open academic single-die process is a comparator only.

variants.label: Open UCLA comparator
variants.description: Its published 64D masks/maps are usable for a labeled lab exercise, never as a vendor mask set.

steps.title: Lock SKU, shank and assembly revision
steps.detail: Start from manufacturer drawings or the explicitly identified academic comparator, including cable, contact count, pad numbering and acquisition mode.
steps.check: Reject configurations that assign an active pixel or mirrored second face to a one-sided passive SKU.

steps.title: Pattern and release an open planar comparator
steps.detail: For the UCLA reference, distinguish metal routing, exposed contact/pad windows and silicon outline masks, then carry the correct shank through release. For a vendor passive comparison these are analogies, not disclosed masks.
steps.check: Require each trace to reach its own pad and the insulator opening to land on its site. Never use the UCLA map as a vendor channel map.

steps.title: Transform planar pieces into an assembly
steps.detail: Fusion reverses a second probe; Matrix uses multiple planes. Keep shank-to-carrier spacing, face normals, pad orientation and attachment clearance in the assembly record. The fixture remains unspecified.
steps.check: Run a location/orientation test through the connector map; a reversed plane is not repaired by renumbering sites geometrically.

steps.title: Use external silicon for the active branch
steps.detail: Store the incoming active-pixel die as an external dependency. Orban et al. demonstrate a 512-channel research die with spray-coated die lithography, metallic shielding, thinning and dry shaping. It is not the manufacturer production record.
steps.check: Do not infer a recoverable ASIC netlist, exact 512-channel vendor model, or qualify a standard spin coater for die-edge spray coverage.

steps.title: Connect to the correct headstage and test continuity/map
steps.detail: A specific passive connector may route to an external amplifier; an active probe can multiplex and digitize on-board. Keep these test paths separate and require an actual pin table before reporting channel identities.
steps.check: Independent tagged inputs must appear on the intended outputs; absent pin tables are unknown, not identity ordering.

gaps: Family-level vendor information does not supply every SKU, mask, lot process or bonding fixture. Patient or animal performance is not inferred.
Commercial SiNAPS and the published academic 512-channel post-process comparison are intentionally not marked interchangeable.

sources.title: NeuroNexus: silicon probe series
sources.note: Manufacturer distinguishes planar, clustered, back-to-back Fusion, assembled Matrix and active-pixel SiNAPS series; documents families, not production travelers.

sources.title: UCLA Masmanidis Lab: silicon microprobe design release
sources.note: The 2017/2019 reticle files, PCB Gerbers and mapping scripts provide a separately attributable open comparator. These are not NeuroNexus masks.

sources.title: Open source silicon microprobes for high throughput neural recording
sources.note: Sections 2.2–2.5: three mask roles, release, assembly and mapping of the UCLA designs, not the vendor’s flow.

sources.title: Orban et al. (2026): single-die SiNAPS MEMS post-processing
sources.note: A distinct 512-channel academic optical-fiber-ready prototype: die-level contacts/light shielding, thinning, dry etch and measurement limits. Not a recipe for all NeuroNexus SiNAPS products.

profiles.title: MultiTransm: two functional finishes on a dual-shank silicon probe
profiles.summary: A shared patterned Ti/Pt conductor layer serves functionally different sites. The on-probe reference, counter, small recording contacts and larger chemical sensing contact must retain separate identities through surface modification.

variants.label: Published dual-mode assembly
variants.description: Two 5.70 mm shanks have unequal widths. The larger chemical contact and smaller recording sites are not exchangeable.

variants.label: Bare and partially coated control sites
variants.description: Use the reported unmodified/partially modified surfaces as comparison specimens, not extra sites on the finished array.

variants.label: Uniform coat on every site
variants.description: This defeats the published selective interface architecture and changes reference behavior.

steps.title: Prepare the oxide-on-SOI base
steps.detail: The work starts from SOI and specifically uses low-pressure CVD for the initial oxide. The register’s PECVD tool represents a later step only.
steps.check: Identify the supplied initial dielectric and its provenance. Do not substitute PECVD for LPCVD without requalification.

steps.title: Route Ti/Pt bilayer conductors
steps.detail: Pattern site, conductor and pad geometry; deposit Ti/Pt layers and lift off. Roles include a working site, Pt counter, integrated reference and electrophysiology contacts.
steps.check: Check net isolation between working, counter, reference and independent recording contacts.

steps.title: Passivate and open the sensing windows
steps.detail: The published top stack is 300 nm silicon oxide plus 500 nm silicon nitride from PECVD. Open required electrode areas before shaping the probe.
steps.check: Register windows over metal and compare film thicknesses separately; an apparent open could be a residual dielectric.

steps.title: Shape and release the asymmetric shanks
steps.detail: Define the silicon/oxide outline, then release by wet etching. Preserve the two distinct widths rather than mirroring one shank.
steps.check: Inspect both released profiles and compare their separation with the device drawing.

steps.title: Apply electrochemical finishes by site role
steps.detail: The electrophysiology and working interfaces use Pt nanoparticles/PEDOT:PSS; the dopamine working site adds Nafion. The reference gets IrOx rather than the recording-site finish.
steps.check: Track the electrode addressed at each deposition and inspect for cross-contamination. Keep Pt counter identity independent.

steps.title: Validate two signals against different references
steps.detail: In a bench reconstruction, compare site impedance, chemical sensitivity and reference drift separately. Add a blank and interference control rather than treating low impedance as proof of analyte selectivity.
steps.check: A simulated electrical tone uses voltage units; a calibration series uses known analyte concentration and current. An arbitrary voltage ripple cannot validate a concentration estimate.

gaps: Exact mask patterns, authorized LPCVD hardware and film chemistry qualification are unverified here.
A site-labeled electrochemical workflow is not a biological experiment. No in vivo signals, clinical performance or tissue chemistry are simulated.

sources.title: Jia et al. (2025): targeted MultiTransm microelectrode arrays
sources.note: Materials and Methods: fabrication, targeted site modification, in vitro calibration; Figures 1–3 distinguish electrophysiology, analyte and reference surfaces.

profiles.title: Transient silicon: cavity pressure and temperature sensor
profiles.summary: A sealed cavity turns pressure into membrane strain. The same silicon gauge material away from the cavity tracks temperature. End of electrical function and disappearance of all material are separate endpoints.

variants.label: Nanoporous Si support
variants.description: A PLGA diaphragm seals an etched cavity on the nanoporous silicon support.

variants.label: Magnesium support
variants.description: The paper also uses Mg foil as a distinct support; the resulting dissolution and mechanical behavior are not the silicon values.

variants.label: External telemetry or separately integrated NFC
variants.description: Telemetry is a different assembly. The demonstrated NFC chain includes nonresorbing electronics; do not call the whole communications system fully resorbable.

steps.title: Obtain defined silicon nanomembranes
steps.detail: Boron-doped device silicon comes from a prepared SOI source. The required doping process is not a registered, qualified diffusion line.
steps.check: Track nanomembrane provenance and reject an undoped-film substitution as a known gauge.

steps.title: Transfer, pattern and protect a serpentine gauge
steps.detail: Release the thin silicon and transfer to a temporary carrier. Pattern serpentine resistors, add insulation, and transfer the mesh to PLGA. A manual stamp/alignment fixture remains necessary.
steps.check: Measure end-to-end resistance before and after transfer; broken serpentine turns are not pressure effects.

steps.title: Form the cavity and laminate the diaphragm
steps.detail: Prepare a relief in the chosen porous Si or Mg support, then align and seal the PLGA film. The pressure gauge must lie at the cavity edge; the temperature reference sits away from it.
steps.check: Under a dummy pressure load, distinguish membrane response from rigid-support temperature response and seal leakage.

steps.title: Connect dissolvable interconnects to the chosen reader
steps.detail: The article distinguishes dissolvable wires and Mo contact films from the external radio or the partly resorbable NFC assembly. Specifying the readout changes the bill of materials.
steps.check: A component inventory must mark the conventional electronics/capacitors as nonresorbing where applicable.

steps.title: Calibrate pressure and temperature together
steps.detail: Apply a pressure reference and known bath temperatures independently to separate piezoresistive response from thermal drift. Register pressure and resistance instruments are bench analogues of the reported fixture.
steps.check: At fixed temperature, pressure should dominate the cavity-edge gauge; at fixed pressure, compare both gauges.

steps.title: Track functional lifetime separately from dissolution
steps.detail: Repeat the electrical calibration over soak time and track material thickness on separate witness samples. Elevated-temperature accelerated behavior is not automatically the same as ambient service life.
steps.check: Record time to loss of calibration and time to measured material loss as distinct outcomes, with bath conditions.

gaps: No qualification for donor doping, transfer alignment, membrane adhesion or sensor lifetime is implied by the register.
This device senses pressure/temperature rather than extracellular spikes. No biological or clinical prediction follows from the bench calibration.

sources.title: Kang et al. (2016): bioresorbable silicon sensors
sources.note: Figures 1–2, Extended Data Figure 1 and Methods separate cavity-edge gauge, temperature reference, substrate variants, transfer process and partially resorbable wireless system.

profiles.title: BISC: flexible thinned wireless CMOS tile
profiles.summary: Unlike a flexible polymer electrode alone, this device integrates electrodes, electronics and wireless interfaces on one custom chip. The authors disclose two real post-foundry paths, with different thinning and dicing orders.

variants.label: Coupon / die processing
variants.description: Separate dies before mechanical thinning/polishing; backside Parylene-C is applied after thinning.

variants.label: 200 mm wafer post-processing
variants.description: Thin the supported wafer by wet etch before laser singulation. Front-end foundry and the reported 200 mm post-processing site are not the same claim.

variants.label: Passive ECoG grid with a remote ADC
variants.description: Not equivalent: the 256 × 256 physical contacts sit on an integrated active RF/AFE chip.

steps.title: Receive the BISC ASIC
steps.detail: The input is a 12 × 12 mm custom TSMC 0.13 µm BCD die/wafer. Analog/digital circuitry and RF design are not made on the register.
steps.check: Hold commercial PDK and vendor wafer manufacture external even though later processing is described.

steps.title: Create TiN contacts and front passivation
steps.detail: Pattern and sputter contact material, insulate the front with PI, reopen sites and add the later TiN layer. The registered 02-01 exposure station is limited to 150 mm: use it as an analogy only for a pre-separated die/coupon in a qualified holder, never on the full 200 mm wafer.
steps.check: Inspect site windows and continuity; verify the coupon holder and orientation before this local analogy.

steps.title: Full-wafer front photolithography: external
steps.detail: The paper also describes a 200 mm wafer-scale flow. This requires a compatible exposure tool and wafer handling; the registered 150 mm 02-01 is physically incompatible, even if its resolution would suffice.
steps.check: Check installed wafer diameter and handling before any design-rule or overlay comparison.

steps.title: Coupon path: dice, mount, mechanically thin
steps.detail: For individual dies, the authors separate first, support frontside-down, then grind and polish to about 25 µm silicon. Inspect for grinding damage before calling the tile flexible.
steps.check: Measure the silicon core thickness separately from encapsulated total thickness; inspect residual scratches and edge chips.

steps.title: Wafer path: support, wet-thin, then singulate
steps.detail: The wafer path uses supported wet thinning and aligned laser singulation. The study’s laser dicer and its stop-on-adhesive capability are external; a generic saw is not the same method.
steps.check: Record thickness map before singulation and alignment to streets. Do not run the coupon dicing order on the wafer branch.

steps.title: Backside and edge encapsulation
steps.detail: Deposit backside Parylene-C. Wafer processing uses an additional laser trim leaving an edge overhang, whereas coupon handling uses a different trimming allowance. The register coater only represents deposition.
steps.check: Inspect full edge coverage and distinguish the front face, silicon core, backside barrier and perimeter overhang.

steps.title: Bench-test RF, channel selection and leakage
steps.detail: Compare a known electrical pattern to the selected response on the matched relay. Separate power/link failures from single-site defects. The published 65,536 surface electrodes do not give 65,536 concurrently recorded data channels.
steps.check: A complete hardware test needs the specific relay, geometry and operating mode; cap concurrent recorded channels at 1,024.

gaps: No TSMC BCD PDK, production chip masks or validated RF relay implementation are released here.
The register does not establish the excimer trim, full wafer fixtures, lossless encapsulation, yield or medical qualification. No biological performance is inferred.

sources.title: Jung et al. (2025): wireless subdural-contained BISC
sources.note: Methods and Supplementary Figure 5: TSMC 0.13 µm BCD, coupon versus wafer processing, two TiN steps, polyimide front, parylene backside, thinning and singulation. Figure 1: RF power and data path.
